mainTopic: Agents buying for partners, the merchant's marker, and setting a price on goods that are not yet finished
overview: The amud opens with the last words of a distinction from the previous daf: in the wine case, the purchase was not in the agent's control. רבא then rules that when three people give money to one agent, whatever he buys belongs to all three, unless each person's money was sealed separately. Next, רבא rules that a סיטומתא (a merchant's marker) acquires. רב חביבא says this is a real acquisition, and the רבנן say it only brings the curse of מי שפרע on whoever backs out. The הלכה follows the רבנן, except where local custom treats the marker as a full acquisition. The גמרא then explains the משנה about setting a price early. רב says up to two missing steps of work are allowed, while שמואל says anything people can do is allowed, but anything that depends on Heaven is not. Each case in the משנה (grain, grapes, olives, clay, plaster) is shown to fit both views, often because the buyer does the last step. A ברייתא on potter's clay, and אמימר's practice in a town where earth was scarce, show that setting a price early depends on the goods being available. The amud ends as רבא begins to explain the משנה about manure.

steps.title: Here the purchase was not in the agent's control
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a distinction from the previous daf. In this case, buying the wine was not up to the agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it was not in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of an answer that began on the previous daf. The גמרא is explaining why this case is different from the one it was compared to: here, the agent could not make the purchase happen by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of contrast is control. In the other case, the outcome was up to the person, so he carries the result. In the wine case, the seller might simply refuse to sell, so the agent could not guarantee the purchase.

keyTerms.meaning: not in his hands, not in his control

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an argument that started on the previous daf. It does not start a new topic, so don't try to read it alone.

phrases.english: Here, it is not in his hands.
phrases.notes: He means the agent sent to buy wine: the seller might not agree to sell, so it wasn't up to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a distinction begun on the previous daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether the result was in the person's control
steps.terutzMaskana: In the wine case, the purchase was not in the agent's control, so it is treated differently from the comparison case.

steps.title: Three people give money to one agent
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if three people gave money to one agent and he bought something for only one of them, it counts as bought for all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Three people gave money to one person to buy something for them, and he bought it for one of them. He has bought it for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling. When an agent holds money from three people and buys an item 'for one of them,' the item belongs to all three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money was all mixed together, so we cannot tell whose money paid for the item. Since it could have been anyone's money, the purchase belongs to all three as partners. The one the agent named gets no extra claim.

phrases.english: Rava said:
These three people
who gave money to one person
to buy something for them
and he bought for one of them —
he bought for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about agents who buy for several people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A purchase made with the shared money of three people belongs to all three, even if the agent said it was for one of them.

steps.title: The rule applies only when the money was not sealed separately
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule is limited. If each person's money was wrapped and sealed separately, only the person whose money was used owns the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only when he did not wrap and seal each person's money separately. But if he did wrap and seal each person's money separately, the one he bought for owns it, and the ones he did not buy for do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבא's ruling. Shared ownership applies only when the money was all mixed together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides ownership is whose money actually paid. If each person's coins were sealed in a separate bundle, we know exactly whose money was spent, so only that person owns the item.
steps.whatToRemember: Mixed money means a shared purchase. Separately sealed money means the item belongs only to the person whose money paid for it.

phrases.english: And we said this only
when he did not wrap up and seal
each person's money separately.
But if he wrapped up and sealed
each person's money separately,
for the one he bought for — he bought,
and for the one he did not buy for — he did not buy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא צָר וַחֲתֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבא's ruling to a case where the money was mixed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If each person's money was sealed separately, only the person whose money paid owns the item.

steps.title: A merchant's marker acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי reports in the name of רבא that a סיטומתא, a mark placed on merchandise, acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: This marker acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. Merchants used to put a mark on goods that had been sold, and רבא says this mark has the power to acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a formal act of acquisition is needed to take ownership. Here, the business custom of marking sold goods is given the power to acquire. The next steps ask exactly how strong that acquisition is.

keyTerms.meaning: a marker or sign put on merchandise to show it was sold

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
This marker — it acquires.
phrases.notes: A סיטומתא is a mark merchants put on goods to show they were sold, even before payment or pickup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הַאי סִיטוּמְתָּא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: acquisition by a merchant's marker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marking merchandise with a סיטומתא acquires it.

steps.title: What kind of acquisition is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law follows from saying the marker acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'acquires' means here. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'acquires' could mean full ownership, or something weaker. The question forces us to define the strength of a סיטומתא.

keyTerms.meaning: for what law? what does it matter in practice?

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the ruling in step 4 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical legal result of a סיטומתא acquiring?

steps.title: רב חביבא: a real acquisition
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא says the marker makes a full, real acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא said: To actually acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא gives the first answer. Once the goods are marked, they fully belong to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, neither side can back out. The goods legally belong to the buyer just as if a formal act of acquisition had been done.

keyTerms.meaning: to truly acquire, a complete acquisition

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said:
To actually acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סיטומתא makes a full acquisition.

steps.title: The רבנן: only the curse of מי שפרע
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the marker does not make a full acquisition. It only means that whoever backs out receives the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: It means to make him accept upon himself 'He Who exacted payment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a different, weaker answer. Either side can still legally back out, but whoever does receives the curse of מי שפרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the marker counts only as a moral commitment, not a legal transfer. בית דין will not force the sale to go through, but it does declare the curse of מי שפרע against the one who breaks his word.

keyTerms.meaning: to make him accept upon himself
'He Who exacted payment,' a curse on someone who backs out of a deal

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views of a סיטומתא. רב חביבא says it is a full acquisition. The רבנן say it only brings the curse of מי שפרע on whoever backs out.

phrases.english: The Rabbis say:
To have him accept upon himself 'He Who exacted payment.'
phrases.notes: This is the curse from earlier in the מסכת: the One who punished the generation of the flood will punish whoever doesn't keep his word.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: לְקַבּוֹלֵי עֲלֵיהּ מִי שֶׁפָּרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 5 that disagrees with רב חביבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סיטומתא does not legally transfer ownership. It only brings the curse of מי שפרע on whoever backs out.

steps.title: Final הלכה on the marker, and the power of local custom
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that a סיטומתא only obligates the one who backs out to accept the curse of מי שפרע. But where the custom is that it makes a real acquisition, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is that the marker only means that whoever backs out must accept the curse of מי שפרע. But in a place where people are used to treating it as a real acquisition, it really acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument between רב חביבא and the רבנן by giving the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the רבנן: by default, a marker is not a full acquisition, so backing out only brings the curse of מי שפרע. But the גמרא adds a condition: local business custom can give the marker full power to acquire. So the result depends on how people in that place actually do business.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: A סיטומתא normally only brings the curse of מי שפרע on whoever backs out. Where local custom treats it as a real acquisition, it really acquires.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in business law, the local custom of merchants can decide whether an act counts as a real acquisition.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he must accept upon himself "He Who exacted payment."
phrases.notes: This is the curse given to someone who backs out of a deal after it was set up, as the רבנן said in the last step.

phrases.english: But in a place where they are accustomed to actually acquire with it,
they acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between רב חביבא (step 6) and the רבנן (step 7), with an added condition about local custom.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the רבנן (only מי שפרע), except where local custom makes the marker a real acquisition.

steps.title: רב: two missing steps are fine, three are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a seller who was first among the reapers. רב says that if only two steps of work are missing from the produce, the seller may set a price, but not if three are missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he was the first of the reapers, he may set a price. רב said: if two steps of work are missing, he may set a price. If three are missing, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה, and רב explains how ready the produce must be before the seller can set a price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is ריבית: setting a price now for produce delivered later is only allowed when the seller already has the produce. רב says produce with only two steps of work left counts as basically ready. With three steps left, it is still too far from ready.

keyTerms.meaning: First among the reapers (the first to harvest)

steps.confusionAlert: Being "first among the reapers" means the seller already has his own produce, even before the market price is set. The question is only how finished that produce must be.

phrases.english: If he was first among the reapers.
רב said:
If it is lacking two steps of work, he may set a price.
If three, he may not set a price.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה הוּא תְּחִלָּה לַקּוֹצְרִים. אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the marker and goes back to explain a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce lacking two steps of work counts as ready for setting a price; lacking three does not.

steps.title: שמואל: it depends on who does the missing work
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that if the missing work is done by people, even a hundred missing steps are fine. If the missing work depends on Heaven, even one missing step stops the seller from setting a price.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: if the work is done by people, even if a hundred steps are missing, he may set a price. If it is done by Heaven, even if one step is missing, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different rule from רב for how ready the produce must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counts how many steps are missing. שמואל does not count at all. He asks whether the remaining work is in the seller's control: work people can do is as good as done, but work that depends on Heaven (like wind or sun) makes the produce not yet ready.

keyTerms.meaning: By human hands (work people can do)
By the hand of Heaven (depends on nature, not people)

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
If by human hands, even if a hundred are missing, he may set a price.

phrases.aramaic: בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם – אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק.
phrases.english: If by the hand of Heaven, even if one is missing, he may not set a price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's rule in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work done by people never blocks setting a price; any work that depends on Heaven does.

steps.title: Challenge to רב from the stack of grain in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting a price on a גדיש, yet a stack still needs three steps: drying in the sun, threshing, and winnowing. That seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: he may set a price on a stack of grain. But it still needs to be put in the sun to dry, threshed, and winnowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using the משנה, which allows a price on a stack of grain that is still missing three steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said three missing steps means no setting a price. But a גדיש still needs drying, threshing, and winnowing, which is three steps, and the משנה still allows it. So the משנה seems to contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A stack of harvested grain stalks
Winnowing (separating grain from chaff in the wind)

phrases.english: We learned: he may set a price with him on the stack,
but it is lacking being put in the sun
to dry, and threshing, and winnowing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's rule from step 9 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that three missing steps prevent setting a price
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows a price on a גדיש, which still lacks three steps (drying, threshing, winnowing).

steps.title: Answer for רב: the grain was already dried
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a stack that was already put in the sun and dried, so only two steps are left.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he already put it in the sun and it dried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by explaining that the משנה's stack was already dried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the drying is done, only threshing and winnowing remain. That is two steps, which רב allows. So the משנה fits רב.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

phrases.english: For example, where he put it in the sun and it dried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גדיש in the משנה still lacks three steps, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גדיש was already dried, so only two steps remain, which רב allows.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: winnowing depends on Heaven
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, even one step that depends on Heaven blocks setting a price. But the גדיש still needs winnowing, which depends on Heaven, and the משנה allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, who said that if the work is by Heaven even one missing step blocks it: the stack still needs winnowing, which is by the hand of Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges שמואל from the same משנה about the stack of grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Winnowing needs wind, which nobody controls, so it seems to be work done "by Heaven." By שמואל's rule, that one step should block setting a price. Yet the משנה allows a price on the גדיש.

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, who said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק,
phrases.english: If by the hand of Heaven, even if one is missing, he may not set a price,
but it is lacking winnowing,
which is by the hand of Heaven!
phrases.notes: Winnowing uses the wind to blow away the chaff, and a person can't control the wind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר: בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering for רב, the גמרא turns the same משנה against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that any work by Heaven blocks setting a price
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גדיש still needs winnowing, which depends on wind, yet the משנה allows a price.

steps.title: Answer for שמואל: winnowing can be done with sieves
steps.stepSummary: Winnowing does not have to depend on the wind, because it can be done with sieves. So it counts as work done by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to do it with sieves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by showing that winnowing can be done by human effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no wind, a person can still separate the grain with sieves. Since the work can be done by people, it counts as בידי אדם, and by שמואל's rule it does not block setting a price. So the משנה fits שמואל too.
steps.whatToRemember: רב counts the missing steps (two is fine, three is not). שמואל asks whether people can do the work. The משנה's גדיש fits both: for רב it was already dried, and for שמואל winnowing can be done with sieves.

phrases.english: It is possible with sieves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the remaining work as possible by people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Winnowing depends only on wind, so it is work by Heaven, against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Winnowing can be done with sieves, so it counts as work by people, and שמואל allows setting a price.

steps.title: The grape basket seems to need four more steps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting a price on an עביט of grapes, but grapes still need warming, bringing to the press, treading and drawing off the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says you may set a price for a large basket of grapes. But the grapes still need to be warmed in a pile, brought to the winepress, trodden, and the wine drawn off. That is four steps!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, a basket of grapes. It points out that the grapes still need four more steps, which is too many for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows setting a price only when no more than two steps of work are left. Fresh grapes in a basket still need four steps before wine is ready. So the משנה seems to go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A large basket for holding grapes
Warming or softening the fruit in a pile
To draw off the liquid into the pit

phrases.english: And for the large basket of grapes.
But it is still lacking warming in a pile,
and bringing it into the winepress,
treading, and drawing off!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גדיש to the next case in the משנה and raises the same kind of challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that up to two missing steps is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fresh grapes still need four steps, which is more than two, yet the משנה allows setting a price.

steps.title: The grapes were already warmed in a pile
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי חייא's reading about olives, the גמרא says the משנה means grapes that were already warmed in a pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא teaches about olives, that the משנה means a pile of olives already warmed, here too it means a pile of grapes already warmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about grapes that already finished the warming step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא reads the olive case as a כומר, a pile already warmed. The גמרא uses the same idea for grapes. That takes away one step, leaving three.

keyTerms.meaning: A pile of fruit that has been warmed and softened

phrases.english: As רבי חייא teaches:
For a warmed pile of olives,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי עַל הַכּוֹמֶר שֶׁל עֲנָבִים.
phrases.english: here too, it means a warmed pile of grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by moving the case one step further along.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means fresh grapes that still need four steps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means grapes already warmed, so warming is done.

steps.title: Still three steps left
steps.stepSummary: Even after warming, three steps remain: bringing, treading and drawing off.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are still three steps missing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: even warmed grapes still need three steps, which is still too many for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing to the press, treading and drawing off the wine are still left. Three is more than the two that רב allows.

phrases.english: But three are still missing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16 as not going far enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the grapes were already warmed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing one of four steps still leaves three, which is more than רב allows.

steps.title: In that place the buyer draws off the wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a place where the custom is that the buyer draws off the wine himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a place where the buyer is the one who draws off the wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in this place the buyer does the last step himself, so the seller only has two steps left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the seller's remaining work counts. If local custom puts the drawing off on the buyer, the seller only has bringing and treading left. Two steps fits רב.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place (where the custom is)

steps.whatToRemember: Pattern for the cases below: first the item is already partly done, and then the buyer does the last step. That leaves two steps, which fits רב.

phrases.english: In a place where the one who buys
is the one who draws off the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by moving the last step onto the buyer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case by local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller must do all three remaining steps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer draws off the wine, so the seller has only two steps left.

steps.title: The olive vat seems to need four more steps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting a price on a מעטן of olives, but olives still need warming, bringing to the press, pressing and drawing off the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says you may set a price for a vat of olives. But they still need warming, bringing to the olive press, pressing, and drawing off the oil!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the olive case from the משנה and raises the same problem: four steps are still left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same challenge as with the grapes. Fresh olives in a vat are four steps away from oil, and רב allows only two.

keyTerms.meaning: A vat where olives are collected
The olive press, where boards press the olives

phrases.english: And for the vat of olives.
But it is still lacking warming in a pile
and bringing it into the olive press,
pressing, and drawing off!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מְחוּסָּר מִכְמַר וְעַיּוֹלֵי לְבֵי דַפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and repeats the challenge from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule of up to two missing steps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Olives in a vat still need four steps, yet the משנה allows setting a price.

steps.title: רבי חייא reads it as a warmed pile of olives
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא has a version of the משנה that says a warmed pile of olives, not a vat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא teaches: for a warmed pile of olives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי חייא's wording, which describes olives that were already warmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חייא's version the משנה speaks of a כומר, so the warming step is already done. That takes four steps down to three.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (a ברייתא or a version of the text)

phrases.english: רבי חייא teaches:
For a warmed pile of olives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 with a different version of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of fresh olives in a vat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct version speaks of olives already warmed in a pile.

steps.title: Three olive steps still remain
steps.stepSummary: Even warmed olives still need bringing, pressing and drawing off.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are still three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again: three steps are still left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing to the press, pressing and drawing off the oil remain. That is still more than רב allows.

phrases.english: But there are still three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 20 as not removing enough steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's reading as a warmed pile
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three steps still remain, which is more than two.

steps.title: In that place the buyer draws off the oil
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the local custom is that the buyer draws off the oil, leaving the seller two steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a place where the buyer is the one who draws off the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as with the grapes: the buyer does the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With drawing off done by the buyer, the seller only has bringing and pressing left. Two steps fits רב.

phrases.english: In a place where the one who buys
is the one who (draws off the oil).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way the meaning is the same as with the grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 with the same local-custom answer as step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case by local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller must do all three steps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer draws off the oil, so only two steps are left for the seller.

steps.title: The potter's clay seems to need five more steps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting a price on the potter's lumps of clay, but they still need shaping, drying, putting in the kiln, firing and taking out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says you may set a price for the potter's lumps of clay. Why? They still need shaping and drying, putting into the kiln, firing, and taking out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the potter case from the משנה and asks why it is allowed, since five steps are still left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same type of challenge, but here even more steps are missing: five. That is far beyond the two that רב allows.

phrases.english: And for the potter's lumps of clay.
Why?
But it still lacks shaping and drying,
putting it into the kiln,
firing, and taking out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה with the same type of challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule of up to two missing steps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The clay still needs five steps, yet the משנה allows setting a price.

steps.title: The clay was already shaped and dried
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about clay that was already shaped and dried.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a case where the clay was already shaped and dried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first two steps were already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking away shaping and drying leaves three steps: putting into the kiln, firing and taking out.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

phrases.english: Such as where it was already shaped and dried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by moving the case further along.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clay is raw and needs all five steps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clay was already shaped and dried.

steps.title: Three clay steps still remain
steps.stepSummary: Even shaped and dried clay still needs putting in the kiln, firing and taking out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are still three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back once more: three steps are still left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting into the kiln, firing and taking out remain. That is still one more than רב allows.

phrases.english: But there are still three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24 as still leaving too many steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the clay was already shaped and dried
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three steps still remain, which is more than two.

steps.title: In that place the buyer takes the pots out
steps.stepSummary: The local custom is that the buyer takes the pots out of the kiln, leaving the seller only two steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a place where the buyer is the one who takes them out of the kiln.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the buyer does the last step, so the seller has only putting in and firing left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the buyer takes the pots out, only two steps stay with the seller, which fits רב. All three cases in this section end with the same answer.
steps.whatToRemember: In every case here (grapes, olives, clay), רב's rule holds. The משנה is read as an item already partly done, and the buyer does the final step, so only two steps are left for the seller.

phrases.english: In a place where the one who buys
is the one who takes them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 with the same local-custom answer used for grapes and olives.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case by local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller must do all three remaining steps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer takes the pots out, so the seller has only two steps left.

steps.title: Plaster in the kiln still needs three steps
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows setting a price on plaster once it is sunk in the kiln, but it still needs burning, removing and grinding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says you may set a price on plaster once it is sunk in the kiln. But it still needs to be burned, taken out and ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, plaster, and challenges it the same way it challenged the oil and the clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, you may set a price only when at most two steps remain. Plaster in the kiln still needs three: burning, removing and grinding. So the משנה seems to go against רב.

phrases.english: And for plaster
once he has sunk it in the kiln.
But it is still lacking
burning, taking out, and grinding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two-step challenge to the next item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission for plaster sunk in the kiln, according to רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three steps remain, which is more than רב's limit of two.

steps.title: The buyer does the grinding
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a place where the buyer grinds the plaster himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a place where the buyer is the one who grinds it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the local custom is for the buyer to grind, so the seller has only two steps left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once grinding is the buyer's job, the seller only needs to burn the plaster and take it out. Two steps fits רב's rule, just like the oil and the pottery answers before.

phrases.english: In a place where the one who buys
is the one who grinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller must do all three steps, which is too many for רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer grinds, so the seller has only two steps left.

steps.title: Why does שמואל need the kiln detail?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל allows setting a price even when a hundred human steps remain, so why does the משנה wait until the plaster is in the kiln?
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said that if the remaining work is done by people, you may set a price even if a hundred steps remain. So why do I need the words 'once he has sunk it in the kiln'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks from the other side: according to שמואל, the משנה's condition seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the number of steps does not matter as long as people, and not nature, will finish the work. Then even plaster that is not yet in the kiln should be allowed. So why does the משנה mention the kiln?

keyTerms.meaning: By human hands, work done by people

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, who said:
if by human hands, even a hundred steps, one may set a price,
why do I need 'once he has sunk it in the kiln'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר בִּידֵי אָדָם אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה פּוֹסֵק לְמָה לִי מִשֶּׁיְּשַׁקְּעֶנּוּ בַּכִּבְשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from רב's view to שמואל's and questions the same words in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'once he has sunk it in the kiln', according to שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If any number of human steps is fine, the kiln condition seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Read it as 'ready to be put in the kiln'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה should be read as 'once the plaster is ready to be sunk in the kiln'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'once it is ready to be sunk in the kiln'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה's words so that they fit שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not require the plaster to be in the kiln already. It only means the plaster has reached the stage where it could go in. From there, only human work remains, which is enough for שמואל.

phrases.english: Say: 'once it is fit to be sunk in the kiln.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plaster must actually be in the kiln.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only needs to be ready for the kiln.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: wait until the clay lumps are formed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says, in the name of רבי מאיר, that you may not set a price on a potter's clay lumps until they are formed.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the potter's lumps of clay, the רבנן taught: You may not set a price on a potter's clay lumps until they are formed. This is רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's line about the potter's clay and brings a ברייתא about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says you must wait until the clay lumps are fully made. Only then is the merchandise considered ready enough to set a price on.

phrases.english: And for the potter's clay lumps.
The רבנן taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹסְקִים עַל הַבֵּיצִים שֶׁל יוֹצֵר
phrases.english: One may not set a price for the potter's clay lumps
until they are formed;
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין פּוֹסְקִים עַל הַבֵּיצִים שֶׁל יוֹצֵר עַד שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's line about the potter's clay to bring a ברייתא on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No price may be set on clay lumps until they are formed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: black earth is common
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי limits רבי מאיר's rule to white earth. For common black earth, you may set a price right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: When is this said? For white earth. But for black earth, like that of כפר חנניא and its neighbors, or כפר שיחין and its neighbors, you may set a price, because even if this seller does not have it, someone else does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers רבי מאיר and limits his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White earth is rare, so you must wait until the lumps are made. Black earth is easy to find. Even if this seller has none, he can easily get it from someone else, so setting a price is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (introduces a limit)

keyTerms.term: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לְזֶה יֵשׁ לְזֶה
keyTerms.meaning: Even if this one doesn't have it, that one does

phrases.english: רבי יוסי said:
When is this said?
With white earth,
but with black earth,
such as כפר חנניא and its neighboring towns,
or כפר שיחין and its neighboring towns,

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹסְקִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לְזֶה יֵשׁ לְזֶה.
phrases.english: one may set a price, since even if this one does not have it, that one does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For common black earth, a price may be set right away.

steps.title: אמימר paid only once the earth was brought in
steps.stepSummary: אמימר used to pay for clay only once the earth was brought into his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר would give the money only from the time the earth was brought in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what אמימר actually did. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר paid once the raw earth reached the potter, before any lumps had been formed. That is earlier than רבי מאיר allows. It is also later than he would need to wait according to רבי יוסי, who allows a price right away. So the next step asks whose view he followed.

phrases.english: אמימר would give money
from when they brought the earth in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר יָהֵיב זוּזֵי מִכִּי מְעַיְּילִי עַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life practice connected to the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר paid only after the earth arrived.

steps.title: אמימר's practice fits neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר requires waiting until the lumps are formed, and אמימר paid before that. רבי יוסי allows paying even before the earth arrives, and אמימר waited for it. So whose view was אמימר following?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If רבי מאיר's, he said only 'until they are formed.' If רבי יוסי's, he said 'even if this one doesn't have it, that one does'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's practice. It is too lenient for רבי מאיר and too strict for רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says to wait until the lumps are actually formed, but אמימר paid as soon as the raw earth arrived. רבי יוסי allows setting a price right away, since black earth is easy to find, but אמימר waited for the earth. Neither opinion fits his practice.

phrases.english: According to whom?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָאָמַר: עַד שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ.
phrases.english: If like רבי מאיר, didn't he say: 'until they are formed'?
If like רבי יוסי, didn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לְזֶה יֵשׁ לְזֶה!
phrases.english: even if this one does not have it, that one does!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אִי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הָאָמַר עַד שֶׁיֵּעָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions אמימר's practice from step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's waiting until the earth was brought in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר requires waiting until the lumps are formed, which is later than אמימר paid. רבי יוסי allows paying right away, which is earlier than אמימר paid.

steps.title: In אמימר's town earth was scarce
steps.stepSummary: אמימר followed רבי יוסי, but in his town earth was scarce, so he paid only once it was brought in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really he followed רבי יוסי, but in אמימר's place earth was scarce. If the earth was brought in, he felt secure and gave them money; if not, he did not feel secure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אמימר agreed with רבי יוסי, but local conditions were different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reasoning depends on earth being easy to find. Where אמימר lived, even black earth was hard to get. So the reason for רבי יוסי's leniency did not apply until the earth actually arrived.

keyTerms.meaning: He felt secure, he could rely on it

steps.whatToRemember: The leniency of setting a price early depends on the goods being available. Where they are scarce, you wait until the goods are actually there.

phrases.english: Really, he followed רבי יוסי,
but in אמימר's place, earth was scarce:
if they brought the earth in,
he felt secure and gave them money,
and if not, he did not feel secure.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וּבְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּאַמֵּימָר עֲשִׁיק עַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local conditions change how the rule applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אמימר's practice fits neither תנא: it is too lenient for רבי מאיר and too strict for רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: He followed רבי יוסי, but earth was scarce where he lived.

steps.title: The חכמים on manure seem to repeat the first view
steps.stepSummary: About setting a price on manure, the גמרא asks why the חכמים' opinion seems to be the same as the תנא קמא's. רבא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may set a price with him on manure all the days of the year. But aren't the חכמים saying the same thing as the תנא קמא? רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's last item, manure, and asks why the חכמים seem to repeat the first opinion. It then introduces רבא, whose answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא allows a price on manure all year, and the חכמים also allow it. If they say the same thing, why does the משנה repeat it? רבא will explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: And one may set a price with him on manure
all the days of the year.
Are the חכמים the same as the first תנא?
רבא said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated opinion of the חכמים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing should not both be needed.
